author: Icemang
content:
Spellpower coefficients are HEAVILY reduced below level 20, by vanilla design. The scaling gets worse as you go down from level 19 to level 1, to the point where spellpower is nearly useless at level 1. At level 20 and later, spells that have scaling get better scaling for each rank as you level up. This is one of the reasons why dps casters excel in level 29+ PvP, and melee are more prominent in 1-19. Yes, casters with SP can be good at 19 too, but you don't get the same value from those expensive spellpower enchants like you do at higher levels.

For example, I have a level 10 warlock. In my research and testing, I found that spellpower was so useless that I put 25 agi on my staff, because 2.46% crit to my wand (plus 2.46% dodge and 50 armor) was worth more than 30 spellpower. If it was level 19 I'd use spellpower, but I personally wouldn't ever make a 19 warlock, I'd just make it level 39 or 49 to get a much better value from SP gear and enchants.

author: Mothra
content:
I can't speak to his practical results, but I've thought about it a lot and decided not to follow through with a mace spec rogue at 29 for a couple of reasons.

The trouble with it is that the "best" non-grandfathered maces (Windstorm Hammer and "Right") are both mainhand-only. Windstorm is the most dps of any 1h weapon in the bracket to my knowledge, but it's only 2.10 speed and 72 top-end. That means it's less damage on instants and also a very low proc chance per hit for crusader or lifesteal (about 3.5% for crus., 17.5% for LS). Maces are also just slow enough that they don't really make for good poison-applicators in the offhand, so crippling is a little less reliable.

I don't think it's bad, but I do think the old standby Zealot Blade with its 10 more top-end damage and closer to 5% proc rate for crus., 23% for LS is hard to beat. Plus you can then have 1.3 speed Vendetta in offhand for consistent crippling uptime. Would be happy to be proven wrong, though.
